📢 Pope Leo XIV, the first pope from the United States, asked the cycling world to remember riders killed on the roads, including people who ride to work or school. He made the request on Monday, November 23, 2026, when he welcomed about 120 current and former champions to the Vatican, among them three-time Tour de France winner Greg LeMond and Bernard Hinault. "Let us call to mind those cyclists who have lost their lives in road accidents," he said. "Among them are professional athletes and amateur cyclists, women and men who chose the bicycle as their means of travelling to work or to their places of study." He also said cycling "offers opportunities to seek out places of silence and contemplation… away from the noise and traffic of the city." After the audience, Caritas Rome and the Vatican's sports association donated 15 bikes to young people in vulnerable situations. 📸 Edgar Beltrán, The Pillar (CC BY-SA 4.0), cropped. Just one day after returning to Rome from his Apostolic Journey to Uruguay, Argentina, and Peru, the Pope held a baby dressed as a little pope during his first General Audience back in the city. The photo, published on his official Instagram account @pontifex, shows Leo in his white cassock carefully holding the child, who is dressed in a white mitre trimmed in gold and a red cape with gold edging, looking out at the square with a calm, slightly puzzled expression. In a heartwarming and mirror-like encounter, the pontiff blessed the baby, creating a charming scene that captivated onlookers and pilgrims gathered outside St. Peter's Basilica.
